judgment_provenance: Agent-authored expert judgments written from issue content and query intent before executing this evaluation. No human relevance review has been performed.
judgment_policy: Grades: 3 directly answers the intent; 2 useful secondary issue; 1 related context; omitted IDs have grade 0. Status/priority intents deliberately prefer unfinished urgent work while retaining completed or low-priority context. Evaluation queries are reserved from tuning. No synonym or learned-semantic capability is assumed.
distractor_policy: Append 5000 or 10000 synthetic administrative records by cycling distractor_templates in listed order. IDs are distractor-%05d, title includes a sequence number, status cycles open/in_progress/closed, priority cycles 0..4. These physical office, garden, and museum records do not implement the software query intents; all are judged 0, including intentional word overlaps such as cookie, graph, migration, and token.
human_review_questions: Do these intents and graded alternatives resemble actual users' searches?
Which missed prefix or Unicode queries would prevent you from finding a known issue?
For urgent-work searches, do the status/priority preferences match your expectations?
Should an unmatched keyword query return nearest candidates or an empty result?
